net_new_delta: Global duration/energy stress is now visibly transmitting into oil-importing Asian FX: Reuters reports bearish positioning across most emerging Asian currencies, INR at a two-month low, and pressure concentrated in energy importers while KRW/SGD/CNY show relative resilience.

evidence.finding: High oil prices and rising U.S. Treasury yields are pressuring oil-importing Asian currencies; bearish positioning is broad but not uniform.
INR fell 0.5% to 96.3150/USD, a two-month low, as U.S. 10Y reached about 5.34% and Brent crossed $100.
U.S. 10Y yield reached 5.342%, highest since early 2002.

conflicts: Softer U.S. inflation/reduced immediate Fed-hike expectations coexist with stronger USD and extreme long yields.
Asian FX stress is heterogeneous: oil importers weaken while KRW, SGD and CNY show relative resilience.
unknown: Persistence of the EM-FX transmission after the next U.S. payroll/inflation releases.
Causal weights among oil, U.S. yields, portfolio outflows and domestic policy responses.
confidence: HIGH on observed cross-asset transmission; MEDIUM on persistence and causal decomposition.
next_decisive_check: Test whether oil-importing Asian FX remains under pressure if U.S. 10Y stays above 5% and Brent near/above $100; compare with KRW/SGD/CNY resilience to determine whether the channel is energy-import sensitivity rather than generic USD beta.

oracle.finding: Promote energy-import sensitivity × U.S. duration stress as a falsifiable cross-asset transmission hypothesis; do not treat broad USD strength as a uniform FX shock.

supermesh_x.finding: Reuters evidence cross-validates rates, oil and Asian-FX transmission while revealing useful heterogeneity; preserve country energy-balance exposure as routing/context metadata rather than collapsing Asian FX into one signal.
